content:
I'll assess each evidence item against the editorial policy and the central question: **"Which recent advances in AI coding agents are useful enough to adopt, and what should developers still verify themselves?"**

The scope covers coding workflows, verification, maintainability, agent permissions, and evidence of developer benefit. The exclusions cover promotional claims presented as established results, and general AI news without a coding-workflow consequence.

All four items come from a single publisher (Cloudflare), so none can provide independent corroboration for each other.

---

**Item-by-item assessment:**

**feed:cloudflare:7003ef6c4acd73c62fce3a69** — Radar UI redesign. Content is entirely about redesigning a public data dashboard's visual layout (bento box → map + tabs). No coding agents, no developer workflow, no AI coding claims. Squarely outside scope.

**feed:cloudflare:8417bba844174a46ac26bf17** — Workers CPU/memory profiling with flamegraphs. Content is about a new observability feature for Cloudflare Workers. It has concrete technical detail and real internal case studies (R2 worker optimization, OOM fix). However, the central question is about AI coding agents specifically. Profiling is a general developer tool with no AI coding agent component. The post does contain one aside ("have your coding agent do it for you") but this is a throwaway parenthetical, not substantive evidence about AI coding agents. The content does not change decisions about adopting or verifying AI coding agents.

**feed:cloudflare:9cb55fd77f332b5cd7a07191** — Logpush Transformers (SQL log filtering before export). Content is about a log pipeline feature using Apache DataFusion/Arrow to transform logs in-flight. Technically detailed and from a single vendor. No connection to AI coding agents, coding workflows delegated to agents, or agent verification. Out of scope.

**feed:cloudflare:a289db51a1e2a244d95269bd** — Deno joining Cloudflare / workerd + celld merger. Content is about an acquisition and runtime consolidation (Deno team joins Cloudflare, merging workerd and celld for self-hosted Workers/Durable Objects). This is infrastructure/platform news. There is no substantive AI coding agent content. The post also contains only vendor and insider voices; no independent perspective.

**Coverage assessment:** None of the four items address the central question. The evidence set does not support synthesis across three series angles on AI coding agent adoption and verification. The next stage must stop rather than fabricate sources.

Every item originates from a single publisher (Cloudflare) and none addresses AI coding agents, coding workflow delegation, agent output verification, or agent permission constraints. The evidence set is insufficient to support even one of the three required series angles. Synthesis must not proceed; a broader candidate set covering independent publishers and AI coding-agent topics is required before an article can be produced.
